title: Madhya Pradesh State Road Safety Policy 2015

gazette.department: Home (Police) Department, Mantralaya, Vallabh Bhavan, Bhopal

vision: Provide a safe road network for all road users with priority to pedestrians and cyclists
Recognise road safety as a core transport service attribute
mission: Reduce road accidents by 50% and fatalities by 50% by end of year 2020
Make the state a front achiever for UN Decade of Action for Road Safety 2011-20

pillars.title: Raising Awareness About Road Safety
pillars.policy_statement: State government will raise awareness among road users and road makers about road safety. RSA and RSE to shed urban-centric bias and address rural/remote areas equally.

Education: Road Safety Education (RSE) to begin from childhood
Road safety education made mandatory in school and college curriculum
Road safety awareness training programs for teachers
Periodic training for school bus and van drivers
Public_Relations: Expand RSE to cover all age groups in urban and rural areas
Use TV/Radio/Print/Film/Outdoor media for safety messages (seat belts, helmets, no mobile while driving)
Play slides and films in cinema halls, malls, and public gatherings
Transport: 80% accidents caused by driver fault - target awareness especially for illiterate heavy vehicle drivers
Target youth for road safety education due to reckless driving and road rage
Refresher training required for licence renewal and heavy vehicle upgradation
First aid training as compulsory component for licensing
Police: Include road safety education and first aid in training modules for all police/traffic personnel
Educate Traffic Wardens, NSS and NCC cadets
Celebrity endorsement for traffic rules compliance
Organise traffic weeks twice yearly in all districts
Two state-level annual conferences on traffic safety
Road_Construction_Agencies: Plan and enforce installation of cautionary and warning signages
Urban_Administration: Display road safety slogans on hoardings at strategic urban locations
Develop plans for installation, operation and maintenance of signalling and signage for town roads
Health: Train doctors, paramedics, nurses and accident evacuation personnel
Spread awareness about the importance of Golden Hour for accident victims

pillars.title: Providing Enabling Legal, Institutional & Financial Environment for Road Safety
pillars.policy_statement: Establish legal, institutional and financial framework for road safety.

key_institutions.name: State Level Traffic Management Centre
key_institutions.description: Integrated with city, district and highway traffic management centres; uses CCTV footage analysis

key_institutions.name: State Road Safety Training Cum Research & Development Centre (SRSTRDC)
key_institutions.description: Interdisciplinary institute with specialists from multiple departments

key_institutions.name: State Road Safety Fund (SRSF)
key_institutions.description: For road safety awareness, equipping traffic police and transport department

key_institutions.name: State Road Safety Council
key_institutions.description: Constituted on 23-05-2015 under Motor Vehicles Act 1988, Section 215. Chief Minister is Chairperson

key_institutions.name: State Road Safety Executive Committee
key_institutions.description: Constituted on 23-05-2015. ACS Home is Chairperson. Quarterly meetings.

key_institutions.name: District Road Safety Committees
key_institutions.description: Formed on 05-05-1988. Quarterly meetings. Monitored by District Magistrate/Collector

key_institutions.name: Divisional Level Committee
members: Divisional Level Officers of Road Construction Depts - Members

SRSTRDC_tasks: Form State Accident Prevention Committee to identify hot spots on highways
Formulate State Road Safety Norms within 3 months of policy adoption
Carry out Road Safety Audits of all major roads in phased manner (first phase: Bhopal-Indore and Ujjain connecting roads)
Coordinate with national/international research institutes (CRRI, CSIR, World Bank)
State_Road_Safety_Fund_sources: 100% of traffic violation compounding fees collected by traffic police
Corporate Social Responsibility contributions from road transport companies
International funding and central government contributions

pillars.title: Road Safety Information Database
pillars.policy_statement: State will improve data collection by stakeholders, establish central data collection centre, and share data in real time.

Home_Department: SRSTRDC to develop Road Accident Data Management System (RADMS)
Improve data reporting to capture accident causes (driver fault, bad roads, etc.)
Multidisciplinary team to visit accident sites for detailed analysis
Science_and_Technology: Host central integrated database in SRDH (State Resident Data Hub)
Data covers Road Safety, Road Construction, Enforcement and Emergency Care
Provide access to Police, Transport, Education, Public Relations, Road Construction departments

pillars.title: Safer Road Infrastructure
pillars.policy_statement: Promote road safety planning at state, city/town and district levels. Encourage safety-conscious design for new and upgraded roads.
new_measures: Variable message signs, CCTVs, Speed recording cameras
Traffic counters cum classifiers, stopping sight distance, signage
Pedestrian railing, crash barrier, cats-eye, edge/lane marking
Rest areas, proper lighting, service roads, under passes, fly overs
50 Kms road grid patrolling, emergency care, breakdown services
pillars.pilot_phase: Bhopal-Indore road and all roads connecting Ujjain
pillars.road_side_regulation: PWD to identify and regulate road-side activities, formulate guidelines for excavation and material storage on roads
pillars.commercial_tax: Liquor shops to be relocated beyond 100 meters from roads (first phase: Bhopal-Indore and Ujjain connecting roads)

enforcement.e_challaning: New technology-based contactless fine collection system
enforcement.RLVD_ANPR: Red Light Violation Detection and Automatic Number Plate Reader systems
enforcement.new_driving_schools: PPP model for new driving schools to address driver's fault
enforcement.GPS_in_commercial_vehicles: Compulsory GPS installation in all commercial vehicles
enforcement.TIMCC: Traffic Information Management Control Centre as pilot in two big cities

pillars.title: Safer Vehicles
pillars.policy_statement: Only safe vehicles to ply on roads; unfit vehicles removed through effective enforcement using modern technology and intelligent traffic systems.

Transport: Raise awareness for voluntary periodic vehicle inspection
Stricter issuance of fitness certificates for commercial vehicles
Police_and_Transport: Deploy CCTVs, alcometers, speed guns/cameras, weigh-in-motion, interceptors
Sufficient cranes for removing unfit/overloaded vehicles
Encourage private vehicle breakdown and repair services

pillars.title: Safer Drivers
pillars.policy_statement: Strengthen, modernise and improve driver licensing. National data shows driver fault responsible for 78.8% of accidents, 73.7% of deaths, and 81.1% of injuries (2014).

strategies.New_Driving_Schools: Modern schools with automobile manufacturers, private sector and NGOs; compulsory training for commercial vehicle drivers
strategies.Testing_Tracks: Sensor-based computerised tracks; track testing compulsory before issuing licence
strategies.Digitization_of_Licences: All transport authorities linked in real-time to prevent multiple licences
strategies.Database_of_Violations: Database for every vehicle, driver, and offence using CCTNS
strategies.Revocation_and_Suspension: Temporary and permanent cancellation for multiple traffic violators; use Motor Vehicles Act Sections 15-21

pillars.title: Safety for Vulnerable Road Users (VRUs)
pillars.policy_statement: Design and construction of all road facilities to account for needs of elderly, children and physically disadvantaged persons.
measures: Pedestrian tracks and foot over bridges
Schools and NGOs to educate children about road safety

pillars.title: Traffic Enforcement
pillars.policy_statement: Madhya Pradesh has one of the highest accident and fatality rates in India. Needs comprehensive improvement in traffic management.
key_measures: Pan city integrated real-time traffic plan in Bhopal, Indore, Ujjain (Phase 1)
Increase transport and traffic personnel in towns with 50,000+ population
Review and revise penalty provisions in Motor Vehicles Act 1988
Criminal case under Damage to Public Property Act for overloading
No exemption in wearing helmets; seat belts compulsory for driver and front passenger
Push courts for imprisonment in grave drunken driving cases
Robust database of all traffic violations and prosecution
Compulsory GPS in all commercial vehicles
Strict checking of overcrowded passenger vehicles
SMS alert service, 24x7 helpline and information billboards for road users
Home Dept: Rs 1 crore award annually to district with no/least accidents - CM's Award for Best Road Safety District

pillars.title: Emergency Medical Services for Road Accidents
pillars.policy_statement: State committed to ensure all road accident victims benefit from speedy and effective trauma care.
key_provisions: Legal protection for Good Samaritans who help Road Transport Accident (RTA) victims
Emergency healthcare facilities at every 50 kms along national and state highways (NHRC recommendation)
State Ambulance Code to specify minimum specifications for ambulances
Deploy one ambulance for every 50 kms of high traffic road stretch
Hospital-based emergency care networked with pre-hospital ambulances for Golden Hour care
State_Trauma_System_Plan: Deploy existing govt and private hospital ambulances via reimbursement model
Heli-ambulance service for transfer to referral centres where required
Police_measures: Synergy between DIAL-100, DIAL-108, highway patrolling and ambulances
Road Accident Relief Services Scheme (RARSS): Crash Rescue Vehicles (CRVs) with hydraulic rescue tools
Reduce ambulance response time from 30 minutes to 10 minutes over 10 years

authorisation: Home Department is authorised to make changes in the policy.
signed_by: Dev Prakash Gupta, Secretary, on behalf of the Governor of Madhya Pradesh
